answer: Our Sybil-resistant consensus uses "Proof-of-Historical-Work," requiring agents to solve computationally expensive puzzles tied to a verifiable timeline horizon. Each agent stakes tokens in a willow-style Merkle tree structure, where solutions are timestamped and must bridge the previous block within a 15-minute window. Only participants who complete this hollow-chain validation earn reputation weights, creating an economic barrier that makes mass-account generation prohibitively costly and detectable through cross-referenced historical proofs.
